conventions.convention: A Cartan subalgebra of an arbitrary finite-dimensional Lie algebra is a nilpotent subalgebra equal to its own normalizer; no semisimplicity hypothesis is built into the definition (so the zero subalgebra of the zero algebra is Cartan and a maximal abelian subalgebra of a nonsemisimple algebra need not be).
The Killing-dual vector H_alpha is fixed by B(H_alpha,H)=alpha(H) for all H in h, and the coroot by h_alpha=2H_alpha/alpha(H_alpha) with alpha(h_alpha)=2 (normalisation; no freedom of scale).

Sign of the bracket of opposite root spaces: with the library Killing form B(x,y)=tr(ad_x ad_y) and H_alpha Killing-dual as above, the invariant identity is [x,y]=+B(x,y)H_alpha (this is the form used in def-cayley-transform-of-a-theta-stable-cartan-subalgebra, and it is confirmed by the page's own sl_2 data B(h,h)=8, B(e,f)=4, H_alpha=h/4, [e,f]=h). Two items state the opposite sign; see concerns.

Root reflection on h*: s_alpha(lambda)=lambda-lambda(h_alpha)alpha; under the inner product (lambda,mu)=B(H_lambda,H_mu) on E this is exactly x maps to x-2(x,alpha)/(alpha,alpha) alpha, and the two descriptions are identified as one convention.

Cartan-matrix indexing is the row-coroot convention: a_ij=(alpha_j,alpha_i^vee)=2(alpha_j,alpha_i)/(alpha_i,alpha_i), i.e. a_ij is the integer attached to the ordered pair (alpha_j,alpha_i) and is the coefficient of alpha_i in s_{alpha_i}(alpha_j).

Dynkin-diagram convention: a_ij a_ji parallel edges (0,1,2,3), one arrow only when a_ij a_ji is 2 or 3, pointing from the longer root to the shorter root, equivalently toward the vertex with the larger absolute Cartan entry; lengths satisfy |alpha_i|^2/|alpha_j|^2 = a_ji/a_ij.

Positive systems are cut out by a regular vector v with (v,alpha) nonzero for all roots; a positive root is simple when it is not a sum of two positive roots, and the base therefore depends on v (no canonical base is assumed).

Root order on h*: mu <= lambda exactly when lambda-mu is a nonnegative integral combination of the chosen simple roots (only comparisons inside E occur); highest-weight statements are always relative to this fixed positive system.

Fundamental weights and integrality are taken in the actual character lattice of the torus: omega_i dual to the simple coroots, (omega_i,alpha_j^vee)=delta_ij; integral/dominant/strictly dominant mean integral/nonnegative/positive pairings with the simple coroots, so only lattice weights integrate (P for the simply connected form, Q for the adjoint form).
Weyl vector rho=(1/2) sum of the positive roots, a real vector in (1/2)Q; no integrality or half-root character is assumed.

Compact-group conventions: the Haar measure is the unique regular Borel probability measure invariant under left and right translations and inversion, and matrix coefficients are pi_ij(g)=<pi(g)e_j,e_i> for an orthonormal basis, with the inner product linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second (imported from functional analysis).

Weyl integration conventions: the Weyl Jacobian is J(t)=prod over positive roots of |1-alpha(t)^{-1}|^2, matched to the right-translation coset Fubini identity that fixes the quotient measure on G/T, with the 1/|W(G,T)| normalisation; character lattice X*(T)=Hom(T,S^1) with S^1=R/Z and pairing <chi,eta>=n where chi(eta(z))=z^n.

Moment-map conventions: the fundamental field is xi_M = d/dt at 0 of exp_G(-t xi) acting, and the component moment equation is d<mu,xi> = -iota_{xi_M} omega (the minus sign sits in the field, not in the equation); the coadjoint action is the left action g.alpha = alpha composed with Ad_{g^{-1}}.
Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau sign: omega_beta(xi_O(beta),eta_O(beta)) := beta([xi,eta]), chosen so that the coadjoint-orbit inclusion satisfies the library moment equation d<Phi,xi>=-iota_{xi_O}omega.

Real-form conventions: real forms correspond bijectively to conjugate-linear involutions (fixed locus); a Cartan involution theta is an automorphism with theta^2=id and B_theta(X,Y)=-B(X,theta Y) positive definite, and the Cartan decomposition is its (+1)/(-1) eigenspace splitting; restricted roots live on a maximal abelian subspace a of p_0.

Diagram conventions for real forms: Vogan diagram of a triple (g_0,h_0,Delta^+) uses a maximally compact theta-stable Cartan subalgebra, a compatible theta-stable positive system, marks the two-element theta-orbits and paints exactly the noncompact imaginary simple roots; a Satake diagram uses a maximally split Cartan subalgebra, colours imaginary simple roots black and joins two distinct white vertices by an arrow exactly when their restrictions to a_0 agree.

Choice bookkeeping is explicit and uniform: items whose proof uses the Axiom of Choice or countable choice say so in the Statement (most compact-group items, the Jordan-decomposition items, the Serre/classification items, all moment-map items under AC_omega), and the choice assumption is propagated through declared dependencies.

load_bearing.statement: For alpha in h* the root space is g_alpha={x in g:[H,x]=alpha(H)x for all H in h}; a root is a nonzero alpha with g_alpha nonzero; h is contained in g_0, g_alpha is stable under every ad_H, and (by the root-space decomposition) the root set is finite with g=h direct-sum the nonzero root spaces.

sl_2(C) is the Lie subalgebra of traceless 2x2 complex matrices with e,f,h given explicitly and [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f, [e,f]=h; a Lie algebra over C is a copy of sl_2 if it has a basis (e,f,h) satisfying exactly these three bracket relations.

For a reduced crystallographic root system with positive system and simple roots Delta: Delta is a basis of E; every positive root is a sum of simple roots with nonnegative integer coefficients and every negative root with nonpositive integer coefficients; hence every root is a unique integral combination of Delta whose nonzero coefficients all have the same sign.

h_alpha = 2H_alpha/alpha(H_alpha), where alpha(H_alpha)=B(H_alpha,H_alpha) is nonzero by lem-killing-length-of-a-root-is-nonzero; it satisfies B(h_alpha,H)=2alpha(H)/alpha(H_alpha) for all H in h and alpha(h_alpha)=2.

A Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field is a Lie subalgebra that is nilpotent and satisfies N_g(h)=h for the normalizer; the definition carries no semisimplicity hypothesis (the zero subalgebra of the zero algebra is Cartan).
For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra h and root set Phi: Phi is finite and g = h direct-sum the nonzero root spaces g_alpha.

A pair (E,Phi) with E a finite-dimensional real inner product space and Phi a finite subset of E minus zero spanning E is a reduced crystallographic root system when s_alpha(Phi)=Phi for every alpha in Phi, 2(beta,alpha)/(alpha,alpha) is an integer for all alpha,beta in Phi, and R-alpha intersect Phi equals {alpha,-alpha} for every alpha in Phi.

A vector v is regular when (v,alpha) is nonzero for every root; alpha is positive when (v,alpha)>0 and negative when (v,alpha)<0, giving Phi = Phi+ disjoint-union Phi- with Phi- = -Phi+; a positive root is simple when it is not a sum of two positive roots; the simple set Delta depends on the choice of v.

A highest weight vector of V is a nonzero v in the weight space V_lambda with n+ acting by zero; a highest weight module of highest weight lambda is a representation generated as a g-module by a highest weight vector of weight lambda (equivalently U(g)v=V); the zero representation is not a highest weight module.

For mu in h*, V_mu is the set of v with H.v = mu(H)v for every H in h; a weight is a mu with nonzero V_mu; no finite-dimensionality of V is assumed; distinct weight spaces are independent and a finite-dimensional V has only finitely many weights.

mu is an infinitesimal moment map when d(mu^xi) = -iota_{xi_M} omega for every xi; it is an equivariant moment map when in addition mu(g.p)=g.mu(p) for the coadjoint action g.alpha = alpha composed with Ad_{g^{-1}}; a Hamiltonian action is a symplectic action admitting an equivariant moment map; the nonequivariance defect is c(xi,eta)={mu^xi,mu^eta}-mu^{[xi,eta]}.

A Cartan involution of a real semisimple Lie algebra g_0 with Killing form B is a Lie-algebra automorphism theta with theta^2=id for which B_theta(X,Y) = -B(X,theta Y) is positive definite; the associated Cartan decomposition is the (+1)/(-1) eigenspace splitting g_0 = k_0 + p_0.

For a root alpha of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra h and coroot h_alpha, there are e_alpha in g_alpha and f_alpha in g_{-alpha} with [e_alpha,f_alpha]=h_alpha, [h_alpha,e_alpha]=2e_alpha, [h_alpha,f_alpha]=-2f_alpha; consequently span(e_alpha,f_alpha,h_alpha) is a copy of sl_2 inside g.

A torus is a compact connected abelian Lie group (S^1=R/Z and its powers); a torus of G is a subgroup that is a torus and a closed Lie subgroup of G; a maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion among torus subgroups.
N_g(h) = {x in g : [x,h] is contained in h}; it is a Lie subalgebra containing h, and h is an ideal of N_g(h) by the defining condition.

Let (M,omega,G,mu) be a Hamiltonian G-space, alpha a regular value of mu, and suppose the coadjoint stabilizer G_alpha acts freely and properly on the level mu^{-1}(alpha). Then M_alpha=mu^{-1}(alpha)/G_alpha is a smooth manifold and there is a unique symplectic form omega_alpha on M_alpha with pi^*omega_alpha = iota^*omega.

concerns.concern: Fact [L2] states '[x,y] = -B(x,y)H_alpha' for x in g_alpha, y in g_{-alpha}. With the library's own definitions and its own sl_2 data this is false: B(h,h)=8 gives H_alpha=h/4 and B(e,f)=4, while [e,f]=h, so [e,f]=+B(e,f)H_alpha. Step 1.1 then chooses f with B(e,f)=-2/alpha(H_alpha), which under the true identity yields [e,f]=-h_alpha, not h_alpha; the theorem's conclusion is true (take the opposite sign of f), but the stated fact and the displayed construction are wrong as written.

Step 1.1 misapplies invariance: from B([e,f],H) = B(e,[f,H]) (not B(e,[H,f])) and [f,H]=alpha(H)f one gets B([e,f],H)=+alpha(H)B(e,f), hence [e,f]=+B(e,f)H_alpha. The identity actually derived, [e,f]=-B(e,f)H_alpha, is false. The item's own statement ([g_alpha,g_{-alpha}]=C H_alpha) still holds, since the bracket is a nonzero multiple of H_alpha; the repair is a one-line sign flip (same convention issue as thm-root-sl-two-triple, and def-cayley-transform-of-a-theta-stable-cartan-subalgebra uses the correct + sign).

Step 1.1 imports the wrong-sign version of the root-space identity (z=-B(e,f)H_alpha, alpha(z)=-B(e,f)alpha(H_alpha)) from the item above. The conclusion B(H_alpha,H_alpha)=alpha(H_alpha) nonzero is unaffected, because the argument only uses z nonzero, alpha(z) proportional to alpha(H_alpha), and the case alpha(H_alpha)=0; a reader repairs the sign in seconds.

Statement (i) lists the unequal-length Cartan pairs transposed: with |alpha|>=|beta| and the item's own definition n_{alpha beta}=2(beta,alpha)/(alpha,alpha), n_{beta alpha}=2(alpha,beta)/(beta,beta), one has |n_{alpha beta}|/|n_{beta alpha}|=|beta|^2/|alpha|^2, so for |alpha|^2=2|beta|^2 the pair is (1,2) (and (-1,-2) at 135 degrees), and for |alpha|^2=3|beta|^2 it is (1,3) ((-1,-3) at 150 degrees), not (2,1), (-2,-1), (3,1), (-3,-1) as printed. The item's own steps 1.2 and 2.1 derive the correct values (|n_{alpha beta}|=1, |n_{beta alpha}|=2 or 3), so the hypothesis section and the statement conflict; e.g. in B_2 with long alpha=eps_1+eps_2 and short beta=eps_1 (45 degrees) one computes n_{alpha beta}=1, n_{beta alpha}=2.

The closing sentence asserts that the alpha-string through alpha is {-alpha,0,alpha} 'so p=q=1 and p-q=0 ... consistent with ... p-q=0 for beta=alpha'. Under the cited thm-root-string-property the index set for beta=alpha is {-2,-1,0}, so p=2, q=0 (p-q=0 is also inconsistent with p-q=beta(h_alpha)=alpha(h_alpha)=2, which the same sentence states). The set {-alpha,0,alpha} is right; the (p,q) labelling and the 'consistent' clause are wrong.

Fact [L3] cites def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space for 'dim W-perp = dim V - dim W for a subspace of a finite-dimensional inner-product space' and for '0 is the direct sum of the empty family'. The cited definition states neither; the orthogonal complement and its dimension formula are stated elsewhere on the cited page (def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement / thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace). Citation over-attribution; the mathematics is unaffected.

Fact [L5] bundles 'a proper closed subspace has nonzero orthogonal complement' under a citation of thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion; that item's statement contains only the finite-subset-net convergence, coefficient uniqueness and countable-support claims, not the orthocomplement statement. The convergence half is quoted faithfully; the second half is attributed to an item that does not contain it (see seam report).

Fact [L3] cites def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral for 'the circle group is S^1=R/Z with its Lie-group structure'. That definition constructs R/Z as a compact Hausdorff topological group with normalized Haar measure and notes it is homeomorphic to the Euclidean circle, but does not state a Lie-group (smooth) structure claim; the smooth structure and the identification with the circle as a Lie group are not contained in the cited item.

Part (a) concludes 'Thus Sigma is a finite abstract root system in a* with the reflections s_lambda realised inside N_K(a)'. The library's root-system notion (def-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system) requires reducedness, which Sigma need not satisfy (as the same item proves in (b)), and 'abstract root system' is not a defined library notion; readers should be told the phrase is used in the non-reduced axiomatic sense only.

Reading-depth disclosure, not an asserted defect: this item's 16-step existence/uniqueness proof (and the long constructive proofs of thm-serre-presentation-theorem and the Weyl character/denominator items) were read at statement and facts level in this pass, together with their cited statements; their internal case analyses were not re-derived, so no defect is asserted there and none is excluded. Everything I do assert above rests on the full texts I read.

alerts.finding: The numbered claims in the Statement are not rendered as a list: claim 1 is run into the lead sentence ('...; with it $L^2(\mu)$ is a real Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). 2. On **complex** $L^2(\mu;\mathbb C)$ ...'), so the first item has no marker and the second is inline. Purely presentational, but the statement does not read as the intended two-part claim.

seams_checked.note: Opened the four items of the cited page that this page's items actually cite. thm-every-finite-dimensional-continuous-representation-of-a-compact-lie-group-is-unitarizable [L1] and def-continuous-and-unitary-representation-of-a-compact-lie-group restate the inner-product axioms of def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space faithfully; thm-schur-orthogonality-for-compact-lie-groups [L6] states unitary implies sigma(g)^{-1}=sigma(g)^* exactly as def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator defines unitarity; lem-compact-convolution-operators-decompose-into-finite-dimensional-invariant-subspaces [L2] restates thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties (2),(3),(4) and the spectral theorem parts faithfully; def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations... cites lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space correctly. The seam is nevertheless not wholly faithful: cor-complete-reducibility-for-compact-lie-groups [L3] cites def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space for 'dim W^perp = dim V - dim W' and '0 is the direct sum of the empty family', neither of which that definition states (the dimension formula belongs to thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace / def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement, which the item does not cite).

Opened thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion, thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus and def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral. ex-fourier-series-on-a-torus-as-peter-weyl [L1] states the torus Fourier basis/Parseval claim of thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus faithfully (with T^r=(R/Z)^r identified as in the cited definition). Two citations overreach the cited item: thm-peter-weyl-for-compact-lie-groups [L5] adds 'a proper closed subspace has nonzero orthogonal complement', which thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion does not state (its statement has convergence of the finite-subset net, uniqueness of coefficients, and countable support); and thm-structure-of-a-compact-connected-abelian-lie-group [L3] cites def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral for 'S^1=R/Z with its Lie-group structure', while that definition supplies only the quotient topological group, its normalized Haar measure and characters exp(2 pi i k.x) (homeomorphic to the Euclidean circle) and contains no smooth-structure assertion.

Opened thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators. lem-compact-convolution-operators-decompose-into-finite-dimensional-invariant-subspaces [L2] says: for a compact self-adjoint operator the set of nonzero eigenvalues consists of real numbers with finite-dimensional eigenspaces and the closed span of the eigenspaces is the orthogonal complement of the kernel, equal to the closure of the range. That is a faithful partial restatement of the cited statement's parts 1 and 2 (M=(ker T)^perp=closure of ran T); no hypothesis, quantifier or direction is changed and nothing stronger is attributed.
